claims.claim_text_verbatim: Based on this formulation, we introduce MedBenchAgent, a multi-agent framework with a Benchmark Intermediate Representation (BIR) that encodes task definitions, evidence mappings, evaluation protocols, and item specifications across construction stages.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent introduces a multi-agent framework with a unified BIR structure

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent separates planning, which derives and verifies the specification, from instantiation, which constructs and audits items under the locked specification.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent separates planning specifications from concrete item instantiation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent achieves a Task-Space F1 of 90.9%, outperforming direct task induction (79.2–80.0%) and prior-guided induction (85.1%); 994 of 1,000 sampled items from correctly identified tasks pass human audit.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent reaches 90.9% Task-Space F1 and 99.4% human audit pass rate

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We further demonstrate portability to a specialized medical domain and evaluate twelve VLMs, revealing task- and setting-specific variation obscured by aggregate scores.
claims.claim_summary: Demonstrates domain portability and uncovers fine-grained VLM performance variations

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results establish constrained compilation as a scalable and auditable framework for medical VLM benchmark construction beyond question generation.
claims.claim_summary: Constrained compilation provides a scalable and auditable framework for benchmark creation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We address this challenge with MedBenchAgent, a multi-agent framework for systematic medical VLM benchmark construction.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent provides a multi-agent system for systematic medical VLM benchmark creation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We cast benchmark construction as constrained compilation, in which the benchmark specification is progressively established from an intended evaluation scope, heterogeneous source annotations, and medical knowledge, with each confirmed decision narrowing the space of subsequent construction.
claims.claim_summary: Formulates benchmark construction as constrained compilation across stages

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together, constrained compilation and the BIR provide an explicit mechanism for carrying semantic and evidential constraints from benchmark specification into downstream construction.
claims.claim_summary: Constrained compilation and BIR explicitly preserve semantic and evidential constraints

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In this way, MedBenchAgent extends automation from predefined medical scopes or question structures to benchmark specification itself, while preserving the annotation and medical constraints required for reliable construction.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent automates benchmark specification while preserving medical and annotation constraints

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In construction analysis, MedBenchAgent achieves a Task-Space F1 of 90.9%, compared with 79.2–80.0% for direct task induction and 85.1% when the same task prior is provided to the direct model.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent beats direct and prior-guided task induction in F1 score

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For correctly identified tasks, 994 of 1,000 sampled items pass human audit.
claims.claim_summary: 994 out of 1,000 generated items pass human audit review

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Model evaluation reveals substantial variation across tasks, imaging settings, and evaluation metrics that aggregate scores can obscure, reinforcing fine-grained benchmark specification as an important component of medical VLM evaluation.
claims.claim_summary: Evaluation reveals task and metric variations masked by overall aggregate scores

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Table 1, BIR-mediated construction achieves 90.9% Task-Space F1, compared with 79.2–80.0% for direct induction.
claims.claim_summary: BIR-mediated task planning achieves 90.9% Task-Space F1

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Providing T0 improves direct DeepSeek-V4-Flash induction to 85.1% F1, while MedBenchAgent further increases precision from 76.9% to 87.0% at the same 95.2% recall, reducing false positives from six to three.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent raises precision to 87.0% and reduces false positive tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All methods achieve 100% EMA on matched tasks.
claims.claim_summary: All tested methods achieve 100% evidence-mapping agreement on matched tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Table 2 shows that 994 items pass, yielding a 99.4% consistency rate.
claims.claim_summary: Human audit confirms a 99.4% item consistency rate

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Table 3, medical VLMs outperform general-purpose VLMs by 6.23 points in Overall Acc. but trail by 2.48 points on AC, indicating that the aggregate advantage is not uniform across tasks.
claims.claim_summary: Medical VLMs beat general models overall but trail on assessment tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: To quantify such changes, we compare all 66 model pairs and find that 12–24 pairs (18.2–36.4%) reverse ordering between Overall Acc. and individual-task Acc.; within tasks, 4–15 pairs (6.1–22.7%) reverse between Acc. and F1.
claims.claim_summary: Model relative rankings reverse frequently across tasks and evaluation metrics

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across these measures, 28–34 of 66 model pairs (42.4–51.5%) reverse ordering relative to Overall Acc.
claims.claim_summary: Over 40% of model rank pairs flip between overall accuracy and spatial metrics

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across four medical VLMs, Acc. decreases by 5.86–17.97 percentage points (pp) and F1 by 6.33–22.61 pp (Table 5).
claims.claim_summary: Image blurring causes consistent drop in accuracy and F1 across medical VLMs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All seven proposed tasks and their supporting-field mappings were retained without task-space revision.
claims.claim_summary: All seven ISIC dermoscopy task plans passed task-space review without changes

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All sampled items passed checks of reference–evidence consistency, task–query consistency, and evaluation-format integrity against the normalized annotations and locked task contracts.
claims.claim_summary: 100% of sampled cross-domain items passed all consistency and integrity audits

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our analyses identify open-ended task-space specification as the primary source of construction uncertainty, while annotation-evidence mapping and item instantiation become substantially more reliable once benchmark semantics are fixed.
claims.claim_summary: Fixing benchmark semantics stabilizes downstream mapping and item creation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together with the cross-domain instantiation under a specialized medical setting, these results show that constrained, multi-agent benchmark construction can support both scalable medical VLM evaluation and systematic study of the benchmark-construction process itself.
claims.claim_summary: Constrained multi-agent framework enables scalable evaluation and benchmark meta-analysis

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together, these results suggest that open-ended decisions about what should be evaluated are substantially more challenging than evidence mapping and item construction once benchmark semantics are constrained.
claims.claim_summary: Together, these results suggest that open-ended decisions about what should be evaluated are substantially more challenging than evidence mapping and item construction once benchmark semantics are constrained.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This separation allows linguistic variation in the query while preserving annotation-grounded reference answers and the item-level entailment requirement of Desideratum D1.
claims.claim_summary: This separation allows linguistic variation in the query while preserving annotation-grounded reference answers and the item-level entailment requirement of Desideratum D1.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results show that the BIR-mediated design primarily improves the selection of valid prediction targets, while supporting-field identification is reliable once the task is correctly identified.
claims.claim_summary: These results show that the BIR-mediated design primarily improves the selection of valid prediction targets, while supporting-field identification is reliable once the task is correctly identified.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Six failures include four VinDr-Mammo finding-type questions that ask for BI-RADS assessment categories and two BrEaST diagnosis questions with unsupported additions.
claims.claim_summary: Six failures include four VinDr-Mammo finding-type questions that ask for BI-RADS assessment categories and two BrEaST diagnosis questions with unsupported additions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These cases localize remaining errors to template semantics and evidence control during generation, distinguishing item-expression errors from the task-specification errors identified in the task-space analysis.
claims.claim_summary: These cases localize remaining errors to template semantics and evidence control during generation, distinguishing item-expression errors from the task-specification errors identified in the task-space analysis.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The high consistency rate supports locked specifications for large-scale item construction while identifying targets for semantic verification.
claims.claim_summary: The high consistency rate supports locked specifications for large-scale item construction while identifying targets for semantic verification.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Thus, rankings vary substantially across evaluation forms.
claims.claim_summary: Thus, rankings vary substantially across evaluation forms.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results support Desideratum D3: preserving annotation-supported tasks across capability dimensions and assigning task-appropriate metrics materially changes the evidence provided by the benchmark, motivating decomposition of aggregate results by prediction target to reveal capability differences obscured by Overall summaries.
claims.claim_summary: These results support Desideratum D3: preserving annotation-supported tasks across capability dimensions and assigning task-appropriate metrics materially changes the evidence provided by the benchmark, motivating decomposition of aggregate results by prediction target to reveal capability differences obscured by Overall summaries.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The consistent degradation indicates that benchmark performance remains sensitive to visual evidence from the corresponding image, despite references being derived directly from source annotations rather than model-based visual judgments.
claims.claim_summary: The consistent degradation indicates that benchmark performance remains sensitive to visual evidence from the corresponding image, despite references being derived directly from source annotations rather than model-based visual judgments.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Representative VLMs show different relative strengths across prediction targets rather than a uniform performance pattern.
claims.claim_summary: Representative VLMs show different relative strengths across prediction targets rather than a uniform performance pattern.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This indicates that the same workflow can instantiate a domain-appropriate task structure under a distinct annotation schema
claims.claim_summary: This indicates that the same workflow can instantiate a domain-appropriate task structure under a distinct annotation schema

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results provide cross-domain evidence for the portability of MedBenchAgent across annotation semantics and task definitions.
claims.claim_summary: These results provide cross-domain evidence for the portability of MedBenchAgent across annotation semantics and task definitions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Evaluation of the resulting benchmark further reveals task-, metric-, and imaging-dependent variation across VLMs that aggregate scores can obscure.
claims.claim_summary: Evaluation of the resulting benchmark further reveals task-, metric-, and imaging-dependent variation across VLMs that aggregate scores can obscure.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This comparison therefore evaluates catalog-initialized BIR compilation against direct task induction
claims.claim_summary: This comparison therefore evaluates catalog-initialized BIR compilation against direct task induction

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent’s residual errors are concentrated in semantic boundary cases, including a redundant BUS-BRA finding-type proposal, a visual-grounding proposal that did not define a capability distinct from generic detection, a shortcut-prone VinDr view-identification task, and the omitted finding-level assessment target.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent’s residual errors are concentrated in semantic boundary cases, including a redundant BUS-BRA finding-type proposal, a visual-grounding proposal that did not define a capability distinct from generic detection, a shortcut-prone VinDr view-identification task, and the omitted finding-level assessment target.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In contrast, the direct baselines more frequently introduce nonvisual metadata, acquisition or marker shortcuts, invalid spatial evidence, or omit otherwise supported visual prediction targets.
claims.claim_summary: In contrast, the direct baselines more frequently introduce nonvisual metadata, acquisition or marker shortcuts, invalid spatial evidence, or omit otherwise supported visual prediction targets.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This distinction helps explain why Evidence-Mapping Agreement is perfect for matched tasks even when task-space precision differs: once the intended prediction target is identified, annotation-field selection is comparatively stable, whereas deciding which targets should constitute the benchmark remains more difficult.
claims.claim_summary: This distinction helps explain why Evidence-Mapping Agreement is perfect for matched tasks even when task-space precision differs: once the intended prediction target is identified, annotation-field selection is comparatively stable, whereas deciding which targets should constitute the benchmark remains more difficult.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Importantly, the fixed annotation-derived reference answers remained supported by the authorized evidence in all six cases.
claims.claim_summary: Importantly, the fixed annotation-derived reference answers remained supported by the authorized evidence in all six cases.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across the complete audit, there were four task–query-alignment failures and six evaluation-integrity failures, with no reference-groundedness or unambiguity failures.
claims.claim_summary: Across the complete audit, there were four task–query-alignment failures and six evaluation-integrity failures, with no reference-groundedness or unambiguity failures.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together with the task-space review and item audit, these results demonstrate application of MedBenchAgent to the ISIC annotation schema.
claims.claim_summary: Together with the task-space review and item audit, these results demonstrate application of MedBenchAgent to the ISIC annotation schema.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Table 10 shows that the cross-domain benchmark preserves substantial variation across task families and model checkpoints.
claims.claim_summary: Table 10 shows that the cross-domain benchmark preserves substantial variation across task families and model checkpoints.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: No single checkpoint exhibits uniformly strong performance across diagnosis, dermoscopic attributes, and lesion localization, and the relative behavior of general-purpose and medical VLMs varies across these task types.
claims.claim_summary: No single checkpoint exhibits uniformly strong performance across diagnosis, dermoscopic attributes, and lesion localization, and the relative behavior of general-purpose and medical VLMs varies across these task types.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In particular, categorical performance does not reliably predict spatial-localization performance.
claims.claim_summary: In particular, categorical performance does not reliably predict spatial-localization performance.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results are consistent with the breast-imaging evaluation in showing that aggregate model quality cannot be inferred from one task family alone, while providing evidence that the same construction workflow can be instantiated under a different annotation schema and clinical vocabulary.
claims.claim_summary: These results are consistent with the breast-imaging evaluation in showing that aggregate model quality cannot be inferred from one task family alone, while providing evidence that the same construction workflow can be instantiated under a different annotation schema and clinical vocabulary.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We strictly follow the protocols of all models that claim to have spatial evaluation capabilities.
claims.claim_summary: We strictly follow the protocols of all models that claim to have spatial evaluation capabilities.

claims.claim_summary: On posterior features, QoQ-Med-7B achieves higher Accuracy than BreastGPT-8B (57.9 versus 54.8), whereas BreastGPT-8B achieves higher Macro-F1 (33.2 versus 25.8).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: FA improves by 27.09 points, while AA, FT, AC, DX, and PS decrease by 9.37, 1.22, 0.53, 4.85, and 7.50 points, respectively.
